p.i: Et Tu Domine qui es semper idem Deus in æternum benedictus, cujus variæ Misericordiæ, & constantes tamen; Tu veteres nostros & quotidianos defectus, nova usque & recenti benignitate restauras, nec renovatos affectus aspernaris, iisdem licet verbis prolatos.
Ne destituamur beneficio orationum, quas recte prius meditatas unita Tua fundit Ecclesia.
Sit Precum nostrarum Argumentum voluntati tuæ conforme, quæ semper eadem, & suggestionibus tui Sancti Spiritus, animorum fervor-
Et jam nulli dubitamus, Te qui tota es Spiritualis perfectio nec affectata Novitate delectar-nec iisdem sæpe repetitis, piis modo precibus of-i fenai.
Has enim varias esse, vel easdem, nullibi à Te vel præceptum vel vetitum: sed relictum pictati & prudentiæ Ecclesiæ, cui utrisque harum uti licet, neutram spernere.

Fac ut in Re Religionis ita discant homines judicia sua pie moderari, ut nec aliis ignorantia sua noceant, nec facultatem suarum præsidentia iis omnibus quærant privare, quæ rite simul & pie in Infirmitatis subsidium adhibentur.

Et cum Errores fere inducant Novitas & Diversitas, Veritas contra in unione, & Constantia servatur, Ne Ecclesiam tuam sineris vel corrumpi erroribus, vel indecoris in te colendo ritibus deformari à diversa & nova invehentibus [?]: sed nec etiam fraudari veritate, unione & ordine, hac fallaci sententia deceptos, statas nempe has Formas Formam tantum Religionis generare.

page.notes: Running head is Greek, set in capitals: ΕΙΚΩΝ ΒΑΣΙΛΙΚΗ. Doubtful readings: "of-i" and "fenai." at the end of a broken word, read as printed but not certain. "delectar-" at a line end followed by "nec", joined as printed; the word may be incomplete in the scan. "invehentibus" is marked [?] because the ligature in "inuchentibus" is unclear. "relictum" has a long-s-like ligature in "ct" that I read as ct. Body text is set in italic throughout.
